items: short and small; enters the posterolateral IVC, often near T11-T12 and above the right renal vein.
usually joins the inferior phrenic vein; their common trunk enters the superior aspect of the left renal vein.
small accessory hepatic veins near the right adrenal ostium can look similar on venography.
duplicated adrenal veins or a shared hepatic-adrenal trunk can alter sampling and dilute hormone concentrations.
an infrarenal IVC or peripheral venous sample provides the comparator for adrenal hormone measurements.
review venous imaging, cosyntropin timing, collection tubes, and the laboratory's labeling and rapid-cortisol workflow.
use ultrasound-guided femoral access and prepare the IVC/peripheral reference sampling route.
use gentle, low-volume venography to confirm the ostium; avoid deep wedging. Cone-beam CT can clarify uncertain anatomy.
enter through the left renal vein and confirm the common adrenal-phrenic trunk.
clear catheter dead space per protocol, then gently sample both adrenal veins and the reference site for aldosterone and cortisol; record site, time, and stimulation status.
use rapid cortisol when available and the index below; apply local criteria and resample if inadequate.
verify specimens before sheath removal, obtain hemostasis, and send results for cortisol-corrected aldosterone comparison and endocrine interpretation.
adrenal vein cortisol / IVC (or peripheral reference) cortisol. Calculate for each side to confirm successful sampling.
higher adrenal (aldosterone / cortisol) ratio / lower adrenal (aldosterone / cortisol) ratio. Interpret only after both sides meet selectivity criteria.

0: with cosyntropin, >5; without cosyntropin, commonly >=2 (protocol thresholds vary from >1.4 to 3).
1: >4 supports unilateral aldosterone excess; <3 suggests bilateral disease; 3-4 is indeterminate. Use the local endocrine protocol and clinical context.

items: Micropuncture set: 21G needle, 0.018-inch microwire, 4 Fr transitional introducer.
Working wire: 0.035-inch Bentson.
Venous sheath: commonly 5 Fr; 6 Fr for the selected catheter setup.
Catheters: commonly 5 Fr Cobra, Simmons 2 (Sim2), or Mikaelsson; attending preference.
Imaging: ultrasound probe with sterile cover; fluoroscopy.
Local anesthetic: lidocaine, syringe, injection needle.
Sampling: 5 mL syringes, labeled lab tubes, saline, contrast, stopcock.
Sterile supplies: skin prep, gloves, gown, drapes, gauze, dressing.
review CT for adrenal-vein origins and accessory hepatic veins. Confirm cosyntropin use/timing, sample volume/count, tube type, labels, and rapid-cortisol availability with the team.
prep, drape, and infiltrate lidocaine. Under ultrasound, enter the common femoral vein with the 21G needle; advance the 0.018-inch wire and confirm venous course with fluoroscopy.

advance the 4 Fr transitional introducer over the microwire. Exchange to the 0.035-inch Bentson and advance centrally under fluoroscopy; place the 5 Fr sheath over it. Retain wire control during exchanges.
advance a Cobra over the Bentson to the IVC near L1-L2. Use the CT roadmap to engage the posterior/posterolateral ostium; vertebral level varies. Do not advance the wire deeply into the adrenal vein.

remove the wire and hand-inject a small, gentle contrast puff. Look for fine glandular branching, often an inverted triangle or Y pattern. Avoid deep wedging or forceful injection: adrenal vein rupture can cause hemorrhage. Exclude an accessory hepatic vein/common trunk; use cone-beam CT if uncertain.

items: use a 5 mL syringe to gently clear contrast/dead space into a separate waste syringe, then collect aldosterone/cortisol samples. Discard volume and sample count follow the lab/attending protocol. Label site, time, and stimulation status immediately. If aspiration stops, ease suction and reassess catheter position.

withdraw into the IVC. If exchanging, reinsert the Bentson centrally and exchange to a Sim2. Engage the left renal vein near L1, then select the superiorly arising adrenophrenic trunk using the CT roadmap. The left adrenal and inferior phrenic veins usually share this trunk.

items.strong: 8. Confirm and sample the left side:

items: confirm with gentle venography. Avoid sampling the renal vein or advancing into the inferior phrenic branch alone. Clear dead space with a separate waste syringe, then collect and label samples as on the right; avoid deep superselective wedging.

blocks.alt: Left adrenal venogram identifying the IVC, left renal vein, adrenophrenic trunk, left adrenal vein, and left inferior phrenic vein.
blocks.caption: Left adrenal venogram. 1: IVC; 2: left renal vein; 3: adrenophrenic trunk; 4: left adrenal vein; 5: left inferior phrenic vein.

items.strong: 9. Obtain the reference and check adequacy:

items: collect the matched IVC/peripheral aldosterone/cortisol sample at protocol-defined times. Verify all labels and both sides' selectivity using rapid cortisol when available; resample before removing access if needed. See Sampling indices in Quick steps.

withdraw the catheter over a centrally positioned wire. Remove wire and sheath, hold pressure to hemostasis, and apply a dressing. New flank/back pain or instability warrants assessment for adrenal hemorrhage.

items: an accessory hepatic vein can mimic the right adrenal vein; confirm selectivity rather than trusting the venogram alone.
avoid forceful injection and deep wedging; stop and assess new flank/back pain, extravasation, or instability.
a deep tributary may miss tumor drainage and falsely suggest the opposite side; sample representative gland outflow.
strong suction can collapse the vein; aspirate gently and reassess catheter position instead of pulling harder.
clear contrast/flush dead space, label tubes immediately, and keep sampling times and cosyntropin status consistent.
confirm bilateral selectivity first; compare aldosterone/cortisol ratios, not raw aldosterone. Cortisol cosecretion can confound interpretation.
